..
Issued at 420 AM EDT Sat Oct 17 2026

Pattern Synopsis: Full-latitude long wave trough encompasses the 
eastern half of North America to start the weekend...bit of a split 
in the trough with energy in the southern end expected to cause 
mischief along the eastern seaboard over the coming days.  A broad 
ridge (+2 sigma 500mb height anomaly) across the Great Basin/Rockies 
and extending north into the Canadian Territories. What had earlier 
this week been an amplified pattern across the Pacific basin... 
anchored by upper lows over the Aleutians and north of Japan...is 
flattening/becoming more zonal with a strong Pacific jet keeping 
things progressive across North America.  Trough axis now east of 
the upper Lakes so stronger north/northwest flow settling in aloft. 
Low level thermal trough runs northeast-southwest from northeast 
Ontario/Quebec across Michigan and into the mid Mississippi Valley; 
-4C 850mb temperatures off the 0000Z APX/GRB soundings allowing for 
north flow lake-induced cloud streets off the surrounding Lakes 
along with some spotty showers (Inversion ~800mb/-7C at APX).
Low-mid level warm air advection already occurring across the upper 
Midwest/Manitoba/northern Ontario which is spreading an As deck 
toward Lake Superior.  0400Z surface analysis shows a 1039mb high 
centered over the central/southern Plains with impressive ridging 
for mid October extending all the way into northeast Mexico (+4 to 
+5 sigma MSLP anomaly).  Surface ridge axis extends northeast from 
the High into the upper Midwest/upper Great Lakes with increasing 
anticyclonic flow.   

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Breezy/windy this weekend with the start of a warming trend: Another 
round of the "Gales of October" setting up for the weekend...as 
surface ridge axis shifts south and the pressure gradient ramps up 
again...this time with a southwesterly wind component.  Unlike on 
Friday...warm advection will suppress mixed layer depths so downward 
momentum transfer will be less efficient.  For today...strongest 
wind gusts expected north of a line from FKS-PZQ with gusts upwards 
of 30mph.  Gusts to 35mph possible along the Lake Michigan shoreline 
areas north of the Leelanau Peninsula...and along the south shore of 
the Upper Peninsula.  Winds will remain gusty tonight due to 
turbulent mixing...with overnight temperatures probably becoming 
steady or rising a bit.  Gradient tightens up even more Sunday with 
a cold front approaching the Lake Superior basin (which eventually 
gets strung out before reaching Upper Michigan).  Though mixing 
heights will be even shallower Sunday there is more momentum 
available...thus more 25-35mph wind gusts across northern Lower 
Michigan (gusts to 40mph near Lake Michigan)....and 30-40mph gusts 
across eastern Upper.  Have re-jiggered marine headlines between 
outgoing and incoming headlines. Have opted to go with a Small Craft 
Advisory/Gale Watch combination for the Lake Michigan zones from 
Point Betsie north...as well as through the Straits and the Straits 
to False Detour Lake Huron zone.  Despite Gale Warnings already 
being up for the open Lake Michigan waters for Sunday...would rather 
deal with the two periods of small craft conditions at the onset and 
separate out the gales which will be more prevalent Sunday.

Expect temperatures to return to near normal for this afternoon 
(widespread 50s).  Sunday highs would have a lot of potential if we 
could tap into 850mb temperatures at or above 12C...but mixing depth 
too shallow for that (and that lack of mixing is why 850mb 
temperatures are so warm). Expecting more highs in the 60s across 
northern Lower...and from 55 to 60 above the Bridge.

Calmer conditions for Monday as the mild stretch continues into next 
week:  Developing east coast system will bottle up the pattern for 
the start of next week...but the big news for Monday will be less 
wind as high pressure establishes itself across the Great Lakes. 
Temperatures will remain above normal heading into the week with 
minimal spread in temperature forecasts.  Highs in the 60s are 
expected through the work week...with parts of northern Lower 
flirting with 70-75 degree highs from Tuesday through Friday. The 
threat for rain next week looks minimal at this point...and the 6 to 
10 day forecast valid from Thursday through Sunday continues high 
probabilities (70 to 80 percent) of above normal temperatures (and 
below normal precipitation).  Not the best news for burgeoning 
drought conditions across eastern Upper (Severe Drought per 
latest Drought Monitor).
